Glossary
2.5D: 2.5-Dimensional Integration. Advanced packaging architecture that places multiple
dies, such as AI processors and HBM, side-by-side on an interposer or equivalent high-
density interconnect platform.
3DIC: Three-Dimensional Integrated Circuit. Advanced integration architecture that
vertically stacks dies to increase compute density and shorten interconnects, but with
higher process complexity, cost and yield sensitivity.

ASIC: Application-Specific Integrated Circuit. Chip designed for a specific workload or
application, including custom AI accelerators.
Back-end: Back-end Semiconductor Manufacturing. Semiconductor assembly, packaging
and testing processes performed after wafer fabrication. Advanced packaging is making
these processes increasingly complex and equipment-intensive.
Bumping: Wafer Bumping. Process of forming conductive bumps on a wafer or die to
create electrical connections to another die, interposer or substrate.

C2W: Chip-to-Wafer. 3D integration approach in which individual dies are bonded onto a
wafer, allowing tested dies to be selected before stacking.
Chiplet: A smaller functional die designed to be integrated with other dies within one
package, enabling system performance to scale without relying solely on larger monolithic
chips.
CMP: Chemical Mechanical Planarization. Precision polishing process used to create
extremely flat wafer surfaces, important for advanced 3D integration and hybrid bonding.

CoWoS: Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate. Family of 2.5D advanced packaging architectures
that integrates multiple compute and memory dies through high-density interconnects.
CoWoS-L: Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate – Local Silicon Interconnect 2.5D architecture
combining an RDL-based interposer with local silicon interconnects, offering greater
scalability and design flexibility for larger AI packages.
CoWoS-S: Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate – Silicon Interposer 2.5D architecture using a

full silicon interposer to connect multiple dies.
CP: Chip Probe Electrical testing of individual dies while they remain on the wafer, helping
identify functional dies before downstream packaging.
CPO: Co-Packaged Optics Integration of optical communication components close to
compute or switching chips to increase interconnect bandwidth and reduce power
consumption.
CSP: Cloud Service Provider Large cloud-computing customer that operates data-center

infrastructure and is an important source of demand for AI accelerators and advanced
packaging.
Dicing: Wafer Dicing Process of cutting a processed wafer into individual semiconductor
dies.

### Page 48

M
Asia Pacific Insight
48
ECP: Electrochemical Plating Process that electrochemically deposits conductive metals,
typically copper, for structures including RDL and TSV-related interconnects.
EUV: Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography Advanced lithography technology used in leading-
edge semiconductor wafer fabrication.
Fab: Semiconductor Fabrication Plant Manufacturing facility in which semiconductor
wafers are processed and chips are fabricated.
Fabless: Fabless Semiconductor Company Semiconductor company that designs chips

but outsources wafer manufacturing to foundries.
Fan-in: Fan-in Wafer-Level Packaging Wafer-level packaging architecture in which
package interconnections remain within the footprint of the original die.
Fan-out: Fan-out Packaging Packaging architecture that redistributes connections beyond
the original die footprint, enabling more I/O connections and potentially multi-die
integration.
Fine Pitch: Fine Interconnect Pitch Small spacing between electrical interconnects. Finer

pitch enables higher interconnect density and bandwidth but requires greater
manufacturing precision.
Flip Chip: Flip-Chip Packaging Packaging method in which a die is flipped face-down and
electrically connected through bumps rather than conventional wire bonds.
Foundry: Semiconductor Foundry Manufacturer that fabricates semiconductor wafers for
chip designers and other customers.
Front-end: Front-end Semiconductor Manufacturing Wafer-fabrication processes used

to create transistors and circuitry before semiconductor assembly and packaging.
GPU: Graphics Processing Unit Highly parallel processor widely used for AI workloads
and a key source of demand for 2.5D/3D advanced packaging.
HBM: High-Bandwidth Memory Vertically stacked DRAM positioned close to AI
processors to provide very high memory bandwidth. HBM availability can constrain AI
accelerator and advanced-packaging output.
HBM3E / HBM4 / HBM4E: High-Bandwidth Memory Generations Successive generations

of HBM with increasing bandwidth, capacity and packaging complexity.
Heterogeneous Integration Integration of different types of dies, potentially
manufactured using different process technologies, into a single package or system.
HPC: High-Performance Computing Compute-intensive applications requiring high
processing performance and memory bandwidth, making them major users of advanced
packaging.
Hybrid Bonding: High-density bonding technology that directly connects metal

interconnects and dielectric surfaces between dies or wafers, enabling finer interconnect
pitch for advanced 3D integration.
Interposer: Intermediate layer connecting multiple dies within a package through high-
density electrical interconnects; commonly used in 2.5D packaging.

### Page 49

M
Asia Pacific Insight
Morgan Stanley Research 49
KGD: Known-Good Die: Die that has been tested and confirmed functional before being
incorporated into a multi-die package, helping reduce yield-related losses.
Logic Folding: Huawei's logic-stacking approach that uses vertical integration to shorten
signal paths and increase effective transistor density through system-, circuit- and
packaging-level innovation.
Micro-bump: Very small conductive bump used to create fine-pitch electrical connections

between dies in advanced packages.
NPU: Neural Processing Unit Processor optimized specifically for neural-network and AI
workloads.
OSAT: Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test Semiconductor service provider
specializing in chip assembly, packaging and testing. JCET, SJ Semi, ASE and Amkor are
examples discussed in the report.
Panel-Level Packaging: Packaging approach that processes semiconductor packages on
large rectangular panels rather than conventional circular wafers, potentially improving

manufacturing efficiency and cost at scale.
RDL: Redistribution Layer Fine metal wiring layers that redistribute electrical
connections between dies, bumps and other package components.
Singulation Package / Die Singulation Process of separating individual semiconductor
dies or packages from a processed wafer or panel.
SoC: System-on-Chip Semiconductor integrating multiple system functions, such as
processing, memory control and I/O, onto a single chip.

SoIC: System on Integrated Chips TSMC's 3D integration platform for vertically stacking
semiconductor dies using high-density interconnect technologies.
TCB: Thermo-Compression Bonding Precision bonding process that uses heat and
pressure to connect dies, increasingly important for HBM and advanced 2.5D/3D
packaging.
TSV: Through-Silicon Via Vertical electrical connection passing through silicon, enabling
high-density connections through interposers or vertically stacked dies.

UTR: Utilization Rate Proportion of installed manufacturing capacity that is actually being
used. A key measure of advanced-packaging supply-demand balance.
W2W: Wafer-to-Wafer 3D integration approach in which two complete wafers are aligned
and bonded before being diced into individual devices.
Wafer Thinning: Wafer Thinning / Grinding Process of reducing wafer thickness, enabling
thinner dies and tighter vertical stacking in HBM and 3D packages.

WLCSP: Wafer-Level Chip-Scale Package Wafer-level packaging in which the completed
package is approximately the same size as the semiconductor die.
WLPL Wafer-Level Packaging Packaging process performed while semiconductor dies
remain part of the wafer rather than after individual die singulation.
XDFOI: XDFOI Advanced Packaging Platform JCET's advanced packaging platform used

### Page 50

M
Asia Pacific Insight
50
for high-density and heterogeneous integration applications.

Japan Insight

Investment Perspective
MLCC is early cycle in AI server & rack penetration
There is immense change underway for the MLCC industry with an investment narrative
that is changing as AI chips/server demand is increasingly driving MLCC scarcity.  AI is
shifting from semiconductors to MLCCs, creating a supply/demand mismatch in high-end
components. The high-end AI MLCC market is effectively a Japanese-Korean duopoly with
Murata and SEMCO together hold around 85% share. High-capacitance, low-ESL parts for

AI accelerators require hundreds to over a thousand dielectric layers with near-zero
defects and face strict customer qualification — the barrier preventing a repeat of 2017-
18, when shortages invited entry and the cycle self-corrected. AI platforms now compete
directly with consumer, automotive, and industrial applications for advanced materials,
heightening supply risk for MLCC traditional customers. We are still in the early innings,
and supply concerns are extending beyond near-term shortages to longer-term supply

security. As a result, we are seeing an increasing number of long-term supply agreements
being signed between suppliers and customers.
Exhibit 1: Sequencing the technology cycle – still early cycle for MLCC
Source:  Morgan Stanley Research estimates
Turning point in MLCC pricing
While Murata Mfg.’s CFO and Executive Deputy President Masanori Minamide stated in a
Sep 14 Nikkei interview that rising production loads for high-end products are making it

increasingly difficult to fully supply low-end products, and that the priority of defending
low-end market share has effectively declined, we believe the company’s fundamental
policy of not changing prices based solely on short-term supply-demand conditions
remains intact. That said, in our view, Murata has been gradually shifting its strategy
toward focusing more on its areas of strength and adopting pricing that better reflects the
need to cover large-scale capital investments, particularly in those core segments where it

enjoys a competitive advantage. We believe that Murata’s reluctance to enter into L TAs for
AI/data-center use value added MLCCs reflects its view that locking in prices today may
not be optimal, given the potential for MLCC pricing to rise in the future.

capacity, high-value-added MLCCs for AI servers/DCs

Key roles of MLCCs in AI/DC
MLCCs play a role in locally stabilizing power supply (instantaneous current supply plus

noise removal) near semiconductors, such as GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs. Since GPUs, CPUs,
and FPGAs repeatedly switch on and off on a nanosecond timescale, they demand large
currents instantaneously, and MLCCs meet this instantaneous current demand by
immediately discharging their stored charge. As semiconductor miniaturization advances,
circuit operating speed increases and drive voltage falls. As voltage decreases, even small
voltage fluctuations risk causing semiconductor malfunction, so even more stable power

supply voltage is required than before. Demand for capacitor capacitance is also increasing
in line with AI servers' rising computing power and power consumption, and because
board area and mountable space are limited, we expect demand for smaller, higher-
capacity MLCCs to persist.

Role of MLCCs in AI servers
Capacitors, including multi-layer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs), function as a “dam” that
temporarily stores electricity, and are an essential electronic component for noise removal

and voltage stabilization in virtually all electronic circuits, including those used in
computers, smartphones, and automobiles. MLCCs play a role in locally stabilizing power
supply (instantaneous current supply plus noise removal) near semiconductors such as
GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs. Since GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs repeatedly switch on and off on a
nanosecond timescale, they demand large currents instantaneously, and MLCCs meet this
instantaneous current demand by immediately discharging their stored charge. At the

same time, MLCCs bypass only the AC component (noise and fluctuating current), which
also serves to prevent noise from entering GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs. MLCCs feature low
ESR (low resistance) and low ESL (low inductance), allowing them to track even

### Page 10

M
Japan Insight
10
nanosecond-level current fluctuations in semiconductors such as GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs. 
MLCCs are often placed around components such as GPUs and ASICs that operate at low 
voltages of around 1.0V. As semiconductor miniaturization advances, circuit operating 
speed increases and drive voltage falls. As voltage decreases, even small voltage 
fluctuations risk causing semiconductor malfunction, requiring an even more stable power 
supply voltage than before. Demand for capacitor capacitance will also rise along with AI 
servers' improving computing power and increasing power consumption, and because 
board area and mountable space are limited, demand for smaller, higher-capacity MLCCs 
will likely continue. 
MLCC miniaturization and higher capacity to accelerate with 
VR200 NVL72
We assume that the space available for mounting MLCCs on VR200 NVL72 will not 
change significantly from the GB300 NVL72 rack, and that the transition from GB300 to 
VR200 will require installing higher-capacity MLCCs within the limited space of 
semiconductor ABF package substrates and AI accelerator boards, accelerating growth in 
demand for small-sized, high-capacity MLCCs. Murata has consistently been a leader in 
MLCC miniaturization and capacity increases, beginning mass production of 1005-size 1 F 
MLCCs in 2000 and 0402-size 1 F and 1005-size 22 F MLCCs in 2020. We expect 
demand for 1608-size 100 F, 1005-size 47 F, and 0603-size 10 F MLCCs to increase 
substantially with VR200 NVL72. We estimate that 1608-size 100 F MLCCs command a 
unit price 5-10x higher than 2012-size 100 F or 1608-size 47 F MLCCs, and we expect 
the shift to smaller, higher-capacity MLCCs accompanying the transition to VR200 NVL72 
to drive a substantial rise in ASP.

High-capacitance MLCCs (47µF+) are likely to capture a disproportionate share of this 
incremental opportunity: Our analysis suggests that 47µF+ MLCCs could account for 
approximately 50-60% of the incremental Cloud AI MLCC TAM in CY27, representing an 
additional ~US$2B market opportunity alone. This reflects both the increasing use of high-

### Page 11

M
Japan Insight
Morgan Stanley MUFG 11
capacitance devices within AI accelerator systems and a growing mix shift toward higher-
value MLCC content.
From a volume perspective, we estimate Cloud AI demand for 47µF+ MLCCs could 
increase from approximately 4 billion units in CY25 to 40B+ units by CY27: Such a 
rapid increase would represent a meaningful step-up in industry demand and could require 
substantial capacity reallocation or expansion among leading suppliers.
Based on our industry discussions, the market for high-capacitance MLCCs remains 
concentrated among a limited number of suppliers, primarily Japanese and Korean 
manufacturers, including Murata, Taiyo Yuden, and Samsung Electro-Mechanics (SEMCO). 
As demand from AI infrastructure accelerates, we believe capacity utilization for these 
products could tighten, raising the possibility of capacity crowding-out effects across 
other end markets and applications.

Materials development and production technology behind
MLCC miniaturization and capacity increases
In MLCCs, smaller sizes and higher capacities have mainly been achieved by thinning the
dielectric and electrode layers (layer thinning) and increasing the number of layers
stacked (multilayering). For high-capacity products for AI/DC, in addition to the layer
thinning and multilayering described above, efforts are accelerating to further miniaturize

and increase capacity by expanding the area of the dielectric and internal electrodes per
dielectric sheet. We believe MLCC miniaturization and capacity increases depend on: (1)
developing superior dielectric and electrode materials; (2) manufacturing highly uniform,
highly reliable slurry; (3) technology for precisely　stacking dielectric sheets; and (4)
technology for firing in a controlled atmosphere without oxidation. For high-capacity
products for AI/DC, we see the key factors as (1) materials development that increases the

crystallinity of dielectric materials while making them finer, in order to thin each dielectric
layer as much as possible (layer thinning), together with (2) manufacturing technology to
precisely stack the dielectric sheets.

Dielectric material manufacturing process
Dielectric materials are manufactured by adding a binder, solvent, and additives to barium
titanate (BaTiO3), which is produced from barium carbonate (B aCO3) and titanium oxide

(TiO2). Methods for manufacturing barium titanate are broadly divided into the solid-
phase method and the liquid-phase method. In the solid-phase method, barium carbonate
and titanium oxide are mixed and fired at high temperature, producing barium titanate
through a chemical reaction at the firing stage. In the liquid-phase method, barium
carbonate and titanium oxide are dissolved in a solution, reacted at the solution stage, and
fired at a relatively low temperature to produce the compound. Manufacturing methods

used in mass production via the liquid-phase method include the oxalate method and the
hydrothermal synthesis method. Barium titanate with small and uniform particle size is
key to smaller and higher-capacity MLCCs. In 2023, Murata established MF Materials, a
joint venture with Ishihara Sangyo and Ishihara Sangyo's wholly owned subsidiary Fuji
Titanium (with equity stakes of 20% for Murata, 10% for Ishihara Sangyo, and 70% for Fuji
Titanium). MF Materials produces barium titanate via the oxalate process and supplies it

to Murata Manufacturing.　MF Materials is constructing a new building adjacent to its head
office plant in Nobeoka, Miyazaki Prefecture, with operations scheduled to commence in
2027. TDK established a joint venture with Nippon Chemical Industrial in April 2026 called
TDK-NCI Advanced Materials (with equity stakes of 51% for TDK and 49% for Nippon
Chemical Industrial), with plans to accelerate development of the oxalate method barium
titanate.

Murata and SEMCO to benefit the most from growing
demand for high-value-added products for AI servers
We expect Murata and SEMCO, which supply small, high-capacity products stably and in
large volumes, to capture the greatest benefits from growing demand for small-sized,
high-capacity MLCCs used in AI servers and data centers. Murata has explained that AI/DC

MLCC sales accounted for 10-15% of its MLCC sales in F3/26 and are forecast to rise 100-
105% YoY in F3/27, accounting for 20-25% of MLCC sales. We estimate Murata's AI/DC
MLCC sales to rise roughly 120% YoY in F3/27 and about 100% YoY in F3/28, with AI/DC
MLCCs underpinning growth in the company's overall MLCC sales. Murata has stated that
it forecasts a 100-105% increase in AI/DC MLCC sales in F3/27, reflecting a roughly 40%
increase in volume and a roughly 50% rise in ASP, but we expect the increase in ASP to

exceed its forecast.
2025 MLCC market share was Murata 40.8%, Taiyo Yuden
11.3%
We estimate that global MLCC shipment value totaled $14.67bn in 2025 (up 10.3% YoY),
with shares of 40.8% for Murata, 22.5% for SEMCO, 11.3% for Taiyo Yuden, 6.9% for TDK,
and 5.4% for Yageo, and a combined 13.0% for all companies outside these top five. We
expect demand for high-value-added products for AI/DC to keep expanding from 2027,
with Murata and SEMCO continuing to gain market share.

What are the risks to Murata?
Risks for Murata include: (1) losing MLCC market share by failing to adequately supply
MLCCs for AI servers/DCs amid rapidly expanding demand. (2) Murata's products,
including MLCCs, are used not only in AI servers/DCs but across virtually all electronic
equipment, including automobiles, smartphones, and industrial machinery, making the
company sensitive to macroeconomic conditions and inventory cycles. (3) The company

has explained that a ¥1/$ appreciation of the yen would reduce operating profit by ¥4.5bn
per year, and the yen could appreciate beyond our assumed rate of ¥155/$, among other
factors.

and losses in the Device & Modules segment to shrink by ¥24.1bn from -¥26.5bn to -

sales in dollar terms (+36.1% on yen basis), a continued increase after F3/26’s +13.8% rise
(+12.6% on yen basis), product mix improvement, and higher utilization rates absorbing
increased depreciation and other fixed cost growth. We expect Device & Modules losses
to shrink mainly due to the falling out of ¥43.8bn in Resonant goodwill impairment and
¥6bn from the disposal of the micro battery business. We project F3/28 OP of ¥702.6bn

(consensus ¥655.3bn). The projected ¥211.8bn YoY growth breaks down as Components +
¥170bn and Devices & Modules +¥39.6bn. We expect Components profit to rise thanks to
a 24.5% YoY increase in capacitor (MLCC) sales in dollars (+23.7% on yen basis) and
continued product mix improvement absorbing increased depreciation & other fixed cost
growth. We look for Devices & Modules profit to rise on factors including increased sales
of high-frequency modules, secondary batteries, and vertical power delivery modules.

We project 2Q OP of ¥125bn (consensus ¥122.9bn). The projected QoQ ¥26.6bn growth
breaks down as Components +¥12.5bn QoQ to ¥126bn, and Devices & Modules +¥13.9bn
QoQ to ¥1bn. For Components, we expect sales of MLCCs for AI/data centers to continue
to increase, the MLCC product mix to improve, and utilization rates to continue to rise. For
Devices & Modules, we expect sales for North American smartphones to increase
seasonally and reenter the black, but because North American smartphone production is

split between fall models and spring models, profit contributions are likely to be limited.

Murata’s share price risk/reward: Even though we raise our earnings estimates for

Murata, we lower our DCF-based price target from ¥12,500 to ¥11,000, mainly reflecting
an increase in our DCF model’s risk-free rate from 2.60% to 3.0%. Murata's share price has
fallen 41% year-to-date from its June 22 peak, and we see 53% upside over the next 12-18
months, maintain our OW rating, and designate the stock as our Top Pick in Japan's
electronic components industry. The reasons are as follows: (1) We forecast the dollar-
based shipment value of MLCCs, where Murata held the top global share of 40% in 2025,

to expand at a CAGR of 21% through 2031, with Murata continuing to gradually gain
market share. (2) Demand for MLCCs used in AI servers/DCs is likely to continue
expanding, and demand for small, high-capacity, high-value-added products, which Murata
has brought to market ahead of competitors, should grow substantially. (3) Outside of
MLCCs, we look for demand to expand for small, high-value-added products, including
secondary batteries for DC BBUs, power modules for vertical power delivery in AI servers,

and RF modules for smartphones, and then expand even further as edge AI devices

become widespread. (4) In addition to earnings growth, we expect that management’s
proactive approach to shareholder returns, including share buybacks, will raise capital
efficiency and lift ROE.
Bull case ¥14,000, 95% projected upside
In our bull case, we assume higher sales of MLCCs for AI servers/data centers than in our
base case, for component sales of 7% higher than our base case, for OP of ¥560.3bn in
F3/27, ¥794bn in F3/28, and ¥1.515tn in F3/31. Our forex assumptions and DCF

assumptions are the same as for our base case. Bull case fair value corresponds to 58.2x of
fully-diluted F3/27 EPS of ¥240.4, 41.1x fully-diluted F3/28 EPS of ¥340.7, and 21.1x fully-
diluted F3/31 EPS of ¥664.0.
Bear case ¥3,500
Murata products are used in all kinds of different electronic devices, and they are easily
affected by the macro economy and inventory cycle. In our bear case, we assume slower
global economic growth rates and lower production of high-end consumer goods like

high-end smartphones than in our base case for OP of ¥314.6bn in F3/27, ¥330bn in F3/28,
and ¥362.4bn in F3/31. Our forex assumptions and DCF assumptions are the same as in
our base case. Here we look for ROE to increase from 8.8% in F3/26 to 9.3% in F3/27 and
9.4% in F3/28, above capital cost of 7.5%. With profit below the market consensus, we
assume the share price falls to a P/B of 2.4x.

FY27 and W8.36tn in FY28, implying further growth of 144% and 47%, respectively. We
expect the earnings acceleration to be driven mainly by the Components (MLCC) and
Package Solution businesses, while the Optics business remains a relatively modest

contributor. In FY27, our projected OP of W5.70tn breaks down as Components W4.56tn,
Package Solution W943bn, and Optics W201bn, versus W1.67tn, W510bn, and W165bn,
respectively, in FY26. In FY28, we forecast Components OP rising further to W6.55tn,
Package Solution to W1.58tn, and Optics to W230bn. As such, we expect SEMCO's consol.
OP margin to grow from 8.1% in FY25 to 15.7% in FY26, 24.5% in FY27, and 25.9% in FY28.
We maintain the stock as our top pick within our S. Korea Technology coverage.

For Components, we expect profit growth to accelerate as AI-server demand drives both
strong MLCC volume growth and a structurally richer product mix. High-end AI MLCC
supply remains tight, with lead times exceeding 20 weeks, supply-chain inventories lean
following two years of destocking, and book-to-bill at the three high-end suppliers
reaching its highest level since the pandemic. Importantly, contract pricing has increasingly
been institutionalized through long-term agreements, while the high-end AI MLCC market

remains concentrated, with Murata and SEMCO together holding around 85% share.
Capacity additions are also unlikely to close the supply-demand gap quickly, as most
meaningful new capacity is scheduled for 2027 or later and suppliers are generally
targeting only around 10-15% annual output growth. We thus expect tighter supply-
demand, higher pricing, and a shift toward high-capacitance, low-ESL AI products to drive
Components OP margin from 21.4% in FY26 to 30.9% in FY27 and 30.1% in FY28.

Bull case W3,000,000
Our bull case assumes ABF opportunities from major US CSPs drive stronger content
growth, with future ASIC content & volume growth continuing to outpace our base-case
expectations. Customer diversification toward non-mobile customers should also reduce
earnings volatility and improve profitability. Our bull case, equivalent to 15x FY27e P/B,
reflects what we see as an unprecedented super-cycle in the underlying AI-related MLCC

and ABF markets.
Bear case W1,350,000
In our bear case, we assume slower content growth in MLCCs and substrates due to
greater competition and China's localization, together with prolonged consumer weakness
weighing on the Optics business. However, we still expect increasing AI exposure to
structurally lift SEMCO's MLCC and ABF ASPs, product mix and margins, given the
difficulty commodity suppliers face in penetrating the premium market. Our bear-case

value corresponds to 7x FY27e P/B. Key downside risks include a significant pullback in

Samsung's mobile flagship cycle, lower SEMCO market share, execution risk in penetrating
Chinese smartphone customers, and continued consumer-demand weakness.

Morgan Stanley MUFG 25
Yageo earnings forecasts
Howard Kao
Tightening MLCC Narrative is Unchanged
We forecast CY26 revenue of approximately NT$183B, up 38% y/y, driven primarily by
stronger AI-related demand, with a more modest contribution from consumer
applications. This demand strength should support broad-based utilization improvement
across Yageo’s passive component portfolio. Pricing is also turning more favorable, with
distributor price increases implemented in 2Q26 and Yageo raising prices for direct

customers in 3Q26, as previously highlighted. The combination of higher utilization and
firmer pricing should drive meaningful operating leverage. We forecast gross margin
expanding to 39.3%, up 310bps y/y, and operating margin reaching 27.4%, up 500bps y/y,
supporting EPS of approximately NT$19.79.
Looking into CY27, we expect supply/demand conditions in the mid- and low-end markets
to tighten further, sustaining pricing momentum and driving an additional improvement in

utilization. We therefore forecast revenue of approximately NT$252B, up 38% y/y.
Continued operating leverage should lift gross margin to 43.2%, an increase of 390bps y/y,
and operating margin to 33.4%, up 600bps y/y, resulting in EPS of approximately NT$32.11.
Why has the stock been so volatile?
Yageo benefited from a sharp increase in MLCC pricing in 2Q26, driven by a temporary
spike in spot-market demand. In our view, ODM/EMS customers accelerated inventory

replenishment amid concerns that the ramp in high-end AI-server MLCC demand,
particularly alongside Nvidia’s Vera Rubin platform, could constrain supply of mid- and
low-end MLCCs. Under normal market conditions, these customers typically carry only 3-4
weeks of inventory. However, supply concerns prompted a rapid increase in inventory
coverage to approximately 4-6 months.
During this restocking phase, ODM/EMS customers sourced MLCCs from both
manufacturers, including Yageo, and distributors. The resulting demand surge drove a

sharp increase in spot/distributor pricing and also contributed to the stock’s strong
performance. However, the pricing move was largely driven by a one-off inventory build.
Once customers had secured sufficient inventory, purchasing activity normalized and spot
pricing began to soften. This, together with weaker broader market sentiment, led to a
pullback of ~50% from the stock’s peak of approximately NT$1,140.
At the current share price, however, we believe the risk-reward has become attractive. The

underlying fundamentals, and, importantly, our view of the MLCC upcycle, remain intact.
Our analysis indicates substantial incremental demand for high-end, high-capacitance
MLCCs of 47µF and above, which will require a meaningful increase in dedicated
production capacity. We expect this to drive further capacity conversion toward high-end
MLCCs, with the resulting crowding-out effect becoming more visible from late CY26 into
early CY27. This should progressively tighten supply in the mid- and low-end MLCC

market and provide renewed support for pricing.

Price Target Discussion and Valuation Methodology
We lower our 12-month price target to NT$1,050 (from NT$1,465): This reflects our
lower earnings estimates for CY26-28. Our price target is our base case value, derived
from our residual income valuation model. Similar to our analysis of other tech hardware
companies within our coverage, we think this methodology provides the most accurate

value of the firm by taking into account the cost of equity.
Our key assumptions are:
• Cost of equity of 7.8%:
° Risk-free rate of 1.0% (10-year Taiwanese government bond yield);
° Equity risk premium of 6.8%;
° Beta of 1.1;

### Page 27

M
Japan Insight
Morgan Stanley MUFG 27
• Medium-term growth rate of 12% (down from 16%);
• Terminal growth rate of 3%.
Our price target implies 33x 2027e P/E and 24x 2028e P/E. These are above its five-year
historical range of 8x to 18x, which we view as justified considering its longer-term
transformation story to become a global total solutions provider, moving from passive
into active components. In addition, compared to global passive component peers, we

believe Yageo stock remains undervalued with higher ROE and margins but lower P/E vs.
Japanese peers (which trade on an average at 40x+ P/E).
Our bull and bear case scenario values decrease by magnitudes similar to the change
to our base case value, to NT$1,490 and NT$480, respectively.

Taiyo Yuden share price risk/reward: We upgrade Taiyo Yuden from UW to EW, as we
believe its share price, having fallen 56.0% from its July 1 peak, has limited downside risk

and offers 6% upside over the next 12-18 months. We lower our DCF-based price target
from ¥12,500 to ¥10,500. This mainly reflects an increase in the DCF model’s risk-free
rate from 2.60% to 3.0%. We rate the stock EW rather than OW because: (1) In its core
MLCC business, we estimate Taiyo Yuden's MLCC market share was 11.3% in 2025, down
from 12.7% in 2020, and we think this downtrend continued into 2026, with its market
share shrinking to 10.7% in 1Q and 9.9% in 2Q. (2) We believe Taiyo Yuden is lagging

behind Murata (No. 1 share) and SEMCO (No. 2) in small, high-capacity MLCCs for AI
server accelerator boards, where demand is rapidly expanding. (3) We expect consensus
estimates for F3/28 onward to be revised down after 2Q results.
Bull case ¥14,000, 49% projected upside
In our bull case, F3/27 sales of MLCCs for AI servers/data centers are 7% higher than in our
base case, for OP of ¥56.5bn in F3/27, ¥85.5bn in F3/28, and ¥176.3bn in F3/31. Our forex

assumptions and DCF assumptions match our base case. Bull case fair value corresponds
to 50.7x our fully-diluted F3/27 EPS estimate of ¥276.1, 33.6x our fully-diluted F3/28 EPS
estimate of ¥417.0, and 15.9x our full-diluted F3/31 EPS estimate of ¥879.1.
Bear case ¥4,500
Taiyo Yuden’s care products (MLCCs and inductors) are used in all kinds of electronic
devices, and are easily affected by the macro economy and inventory cycle. In our bear
case, we assume slower global economic growth rates and lower production of high-end

consumer goods like high-end smartphones than in our base case, for OP of ¥39.2bn in
F3/27, ¥56.1bn in F3/28, and ¥65.8bn in F3/31. Our forex assumptions and DCF
assumptions are the same as in our base case. Here we look for ROE of 7.3% in F3/27 and
10.1% in F3/28, improving to a level above capital cost of 7.9%. With profit below market
expectations, we assume the share price falls to a P/B of 1.8x.

Global Research
First Read
Delta Electronics
Add to APAC Key Call Buy - Taiwan Summit
reaffirms the AI Power opportunity
Capturing a robust industry TAM as the leading server power supplier
Delta affirmed a stronger growth profile as AI infrastructure now is over 50% of sales.
Our bottom-up model from our APAC Focus (link) estimates a 69% CAGR to US$91.1bn
AI server power TAM from 2025-2030 even moderating 2028-30 for hyperscale cash

flow and grid power constraints. We see a strong 2027 driven by +65% YoY accelerator
die growth, Rubin's ~60% higher rack power and AMD's move to rack-scale systems.
400V/800V becomes a larger driver in 2028-29 as rising power density outgrows low-
voltage distribution. We believe Delta is key beneficiary with its  broad grid-to-chip
portfolio helping sustain its ~40% share of a rising TAM.
Near-term supply constraints bottoming from Aug and accelerating into Q4.

Supply constraints on Power ICs have tempered Q3 growth from +15-20% QoQ to +10-
12% QoQ but should grow in Sep and accelerate to double digit QoQ in Q426 and
above seasonal Q127 (UBS +3% QoQ) into new ASIC/GPU platform ramps and more
supply. Management expects shortages to persist for at least the next several quarters
with demand accelerating faster than supply and the supply-demand gap likely
widening before narrowing but price hikes rebounding OpMs.

HVDC Adoption Appears Increasingly Inevitable.
HVDC production and shipments have begun and should be modest in 2027 before
ramping sharper in the following 1-2 years. As rack power rises from 140kW on GB300
to nearly 250kW on VR200 and potentially higher on Rubin Ultra, management expects
space and efficiency constraints to shift power systems out of racks and into side-car or
centralized architectures. Delta sees HVDC as the logical solution for power-loss,

thermal, and density challenges, with higher-voltage architectures offering multiple-
times higher value per watt than current solutions. Delta sees three hyperscalers
evaluating 400V, two adopting it for NVIDIA racks initially before converging on 800V.
Reiterate Buy and PT NT$2,750
Delta's stock has pulled back 36% since May following push-outs to NVIDIA's
architecture slowing the dedicated power rack ramp-up and elevating supply
constraints, pulling it back to 22x/17x 2026-27 EPS. We now see better entry with sales

ramping in H226, spec upgrades to ASIC power racks and Rubin at 60% higher TDP over
Blackwell and margins holding better than feared. The company should leverage its
strong product line, R&D and field support to participate in the key power architecture
transitions in the coming years moving the power stack out of the rack and also
developing emerging nascent technologies including SST for facility level power
transformation and rectification and fuel cells licensing Ceres for medium-term

opportunity to supplement the power grid constraint with alternative energy.

Company Description
Delta Electronics provides computer switching power supply solutions, as well as video display
and electronics components, for computers, smartphones, telecom and industrial products.
Founded in 1971, the firm has production bases in Taiwan, China, Thailand and India. In

2023, its power electronics, infrastructure and automation segments contributed 62%, 25%
and 13% of revenue, respectively.
UBS EPS and Consensus EPS
The UBS EPS is an adjusted diluted EPS metric. It is calculated using the UBS analyst's
interpretation of earnings suitable for valuation purposes divided by the diluted number of
shares. This may differ to the way the consensus EPS metric has been calculated.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We base our price target on PE multiple valuation.

Delta's businesses include SPS and components for a variety of end-applications, video
displays and data networking subsystem and system products. Any changes in these end-
markets could affect our forecasts for Delta. Investment risk could increase/decrease on any
deviation from our expectations for end-market demand and competition.
Downside risks for Delta include: severe supply chain constraints; weaker-than-expected PC/
server demand; a slower-than-expected IA recovery; and a slower ramp of 5G in 2022.

Investing in structured investments involves significant risks. For a detailed discussion of the risks involved in investing in any particular structured investment, you must read

the relevant offering materials for that investment. Structured investments are unsecured obligations of a particular issuer with returns linked to the performance of an
underlying asset. Depending on the terms of the investment, investors could lose all or a substantial portion of their investment based on the performance of the underlying
asset. Investors could also lose their entire investment if the issuer becomes insolvent. UBS does not guarantee in any way the obligations or the financial condition of any

issuer or the accuracy of any financial information provided by any issuer. Structured investments are not traditional investments and investing in a structured investment is
not equivalent to investing directly in the underlying asset. Structured investments may have limited or no liquidity, and investors should be prepared to hold their investment
to maturity. The return of structured investments may be limited by a maximum gain, participation rate or other feature. Structured investments may include call features and,

if a structured investment is called early, investors would not earn any further return and may not be able to reinvest in similar investments with similar terms. Structured
investments include costs and fees which are generally embedded in the price of the investment. The tax treatment of a structured investment may be complex and may differ
from a direct investment in the underlying asset. UBS and its employees do not provide tax advice. Investors should consult their own tax advisor about their own tax situation

before investing in any securities.

First Read
Voltronic Power
UBS Taiwan Summit 2026 key takeaways:
Earnings growth hinges on UPS/HVDC deliveries
Sales turning to growth in H226; sales mix change driving margin expansion
Management indicated bookings and shipments remained solid in July-Aug despite
temporary PCB shortages, and it expects a sales turnaround to growth in H226. Inverter
sales could stay weak on competition and Voltronic's product portfolio adjustments

(reducing low-margin products). Meanwhile, increasing outsourcing by brands will
support UPS sales growth. Management expects HVDC products to start contributing in
2027. Voltronic added a third customer for HVDC products. We think a higher sales
portion from UPS/HVDC products and inverter product adjustments could bring GM
expansion in 2027.
UPS growth intact;  HVDC and PDU represent the next legs of growth
The company expects sales to resume growth by single digits  in H226  and expects >10%

YoY growth in 2027. Management remains cautious about solar  inverters due to intense
competition from Chinese peers and expects inverter sales to decline as Voltronic adjusts
its product portfolio, focusing more on commercial solar  and premium products. For
2027, management expects offline UPS to grow 0-5%, supported by outsourcing
opportunities and emerging market demand, which could offset notebook weakness.
High-power UPS could account for an increasingly higher sales portion, driven by

accelerating outsourcing by tier 1 customers. For HVDC, management highlighted it
obtained one more client. HVDC product progress is on schedule, with 800VDC power
shelf sampling expected by year-end, a pilot run in H127 and mass production in H227.
The company is preparing testing and production equipment at factories in Taiwan and
China. Over the longer term, management also sees opportunities in PDUs, a market it
estimates at US$5bn in 2025, with a 12-15% sales CAGR over the next 5-8 years.

Margin  improvement on product mix optimisation and higher prices
Voltronic has implemented two UPS price increases this year to offset higher raw
material costs, which it expects to be reflected on its P&L starting in Sept 2026. For solar
inverters, management plans to focus on higher power and premium products with a
GM above 20%, while reducing low-power products with a GM at or below 20% over
the next two to three quarters, which could support GM expansion. In upcoming

quarters, solar inverter products may shrink to <20% of the total sales mix, while higher-
margin businesses such as high-power UPS and HVDC products continue to ramp. We
think the sales mix change will expand margins in 2027.
Valuation: Maintain Buy rating and PT of NT$1,128
We maintain our Buy rating and price target of NT$1,128, based on sum-of-the-parts
analysis, applying 28x/23x/24x 2027E PE for UPS/inverter/PSU business, respectively.

Company Description
Founded in 2008, Voltronic is a leading ODM for uninterruptible power supply (UPS) and
inverters. Its major customers include Schneider, Vertiv, and Riello. Voltronic is headquartered
in Taiwan and has production plants in mainland China, Vietnam, and Taiwan.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement

We base our price target on sum of the parts.
We believe the key risks for Voltronic include: 1) a slower-than-expected outsourcing trend
from leading branded UPS companies; 2) a faster-than-expected ramp-up of the electricity
grid in developing countries resulting in lower-than-expected demand for off-grid solar
systems; 3) FX risks; and 4) rising raw material prices.
Key industry-specific risks include: 1) unexpected changes in the underlying global

macroeconomic environment; 2) currency and interest rate movement; and 3) commodity
price inflation.

underlying asset. Depending on the terms of the investment, investors could lose all or a substantial portion of their investment based on the performance of the underlying
asset. Investors could also lose their entire investment if the issuer becomes insolvent. UBS does not guarantee in any way the obligations or the financial condition of any

issuer or the accuracy of any financial information provided by any issuer. Structured investments are not traditional investments and investing in a structured investment is
not equivalent to investing directly in the underlying asset. Structured investments may have limited or no liquidity, and investors should be prepared to hold their investment
to maturity. The return of structured investments may be limited by a maximum gain, participation rate or other feature. Structured investments may include call features and,

if a structured investment is called early, investors would not earn any further return and may not be able to reinvest in similar investments with similar terms. Structured
investments include costs and fees which are generally embedded in the price of the investment. The tax treatment of a structured investment may be complex and may differ
from a direct investment in the underlying asset. UBS and its employees do not provide tax advice. Investors should consult their own tax advisor about their own tax situation

## Document 099: 260921_daiwa_winway

Source PDF: all report pdf/260921_daiwa_winway.pdf
Report source: line報告備份
Date: 2026-09-21
Pages: 7
Extraction status: ok

### Page 1

Taiwan Information Technology

What’s new: We provide an update on Winway’s business outlook.

What’s the impact: Marked revenue upside, but a more conservative 
gross margin outlook. We raise our 3Q26 revenue forecast by 9.3% to 
TWD5.0bn (+177.8% YoY) to reflect the stronger-than-expected execution 
of capacity expansion at Renwu Phase 1. Management guided for flat QoQ 
revenue in 4Q26, due to: 1) seasonality; 2) existing capacity being nearly 
fully utilised, with additional capacity scheduled to come online in 1H27; 
and 3) potential revenue recognition delays into 1H27 to accommodate 
customers’ schedules. On profitability, we lower our 3Q26E gross margin 
by 1.8pp, as we expect higher revenue contribution from probe cards and 
incremental depreciation from the new plant to dilute margins. Overall, for 
2026E and 2027E, we raise our revenue by 3.2% and 0.9%, while lowering 
our gross margin by 1.2pp and 1.7pp, respectively.

Probe card share concerns appear overdone. In response to concerns 
over probe card order losses, we believe the expanding TAM will attract 
competitors; the key differentiator is whether suppliers can scale capacity 
to meet customers’ demands. Winway does not expect its probe card share 
at its largest customer to decline and remains confident in maintaining its 
market-leading position. Its Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) 
probe card supply agreement with Technoprobe (TPRO IM, Not Rated) 
remains in place, which should support its technology competitiveness.

Socket capacity expansion remains on track. Winway doubled its socket 
capacity YoY in 2026 and remains on track to reach monthly pogo-pin 
capacity of 14m units by 1H27, per management. We estimate monthly 
capacity to grow further to 16-18m units by end-2027. Management’s long-
term target is to raise its pogo-pin self-sufficiency ratio to 50-60%, which 
should support gross margin expansion through greater vertical integration.

What we recommend: We slightly raise revenue top-line but lower our 
2026-28E EPS by 1-5% to factor in conservative gross margin 
assumptions. We reaffirm our Buy (1) call, with 12M TP of TWD10,000, 
based on a PER of 50x, applied to our 2027E forward EPS. Our 2026-28E 
EPS CAGR of 100% makes our target PER undemanding, given that the 
resulting PEG ratio is 0.5x. Key downside risks: intensifying competition.

How we differ: Our revised 2026-27E EPS are now roughly in line with 
consensus, reflecting a more prudent gross margin. While market noise 
persists, we see no structural threat to Winway's leading position in sockets 
and probe cards.

21 September 2026

Capacity ramp drives revenue upside

➢ Revenue upside with more prudent gross margin assumptions 
➢ Probe card position intact; socket expansion on track 
➢ Reaffirming Buy (1) rating with an unchanged 12M TP of TWD10,000

Company profile 
Founded in Kaohsiung in 2001, WinWay has evolved from an optoelectronic test-fixture supplier into a 
leading logic test-interface provider. Its portfolio includes test sockets, MEMS probe cards and contact 
elements. Growth is driven by increasing AI/HPC testing complexity, GPU and ASIC design wins, 
expanding SLT adoption and next-generation HyperSocket solutions.

Source:                         Trendforce, Morgan Stanley Research
TV panel prices stayed flat MoM in September: Mainstream 32", 43", 55", 65" and
75" TV panel prices all stood flat for the month of September,  in line with our
expectations. While the overall TV panel demand was lackluster, there is still some
seasonal demand as brands are preparing for year-end promotions. Recently, the
major Chinese panel makers have notified their customers of price hikes from

September/October in order to mitigate increasing margin pressure caused by rising
costs of various components, including driver ICs, glass substrates and PCB.
Although major Chinese panel makers might leverage their annual maintenance of
three to seven days during October 2026 as a bargaining chip, we think it might take
more negotiations with brand customers before they can really raise panel prices,
since order momentum will slow down in the coming months. On a quarterly

average basis, TV panel prices  declined in the low-single-digits % QoQ in 3Q26.
IT panel prices were flat MoM in  September: Monitor and notebook panel prices
stayed flat MoM during the month. Both applications continues to  see slower
demand in  2H26 post the earlier restocking  in 1H26 amid concerns about  increasing
component costs. That said, panel makers are under cost pressure and reluctant to
given more price concessions. On a quarterly average basis, we expect IT panel

prices to remain flat QoQ in 3Q26.
Risk/reward less attractive: We think that the current valuation of Taiwanese panel
makers, AUO (2409.TW) and Innolux (3481.TW) both at 1.7x P/B, has already baked
in some expectations of glass in advanced packaging for revenue contribution in
2028. However, some supply chain players think this might take longer, and there
seem to be more suppliers from different supply chains vying for this opportunity. In
China, while expectations are also building for the glass core substrate, we have a

relative preference for BOE (000725.SZ; 1.5x P/B) over TCL (000100.SZ; 1.8x P/B),
on its scale advantage and faster progress in glass core substrates.

Key Takeaways
Current valuation of 1.5-2.0x P/B have already priced in the expectation of glass
in advanced packaging from 2H28.
Nonetheless,  the risk in commercialization and competition are worth monitoring.

TV Panel Prices Trending Down from 3Q26
TV panel prices started to edge up at the beginning of this year, rising 1% MoM in January,
2% MoM in February and 2% MoM in March. April, May and June were largely flat, while
July was down 2% MoM, August was down 1% MoM, and September was flat MoM,   in line
with our expectation that TV panel prices would start trending down from 3Q26.  That
said, we do not expect a significant decline as supply-side discipline should provide

downside support.

Below-seasonal Panel Shipments in 2H26
Over the past decade, TV panel shipments have typically been split 49%:51% between 1H
and 2H. In 2026, we expect the mix to skew toward 1H, as TV brands restocked ahead of
major promotional events, including the Winter Olympics in February, the FIFA World Cup
in June-July, and China's 618 shopping festival. We see no clear evidence that these events

will materially boost global TV demand, but they have historically shifted shipment timing
across quarters. As a result, we expect the restocking momentum seen since the start of
the year to fade, with panel order momentum slowing in 2H26.
Display Fab Utilization  at ~85% in 3Q26
Stronger TV panel shipments supported display fab utilization of ~80% in 4Q24 and 82%
in 1Q25. Utilization declined to 78% in 2Q25 as brands adopted a more cautious stance

following earlier pull-ins and as the impact of China's trade-in program moderated.
Utilization rebounded to 80-85% in 3Q25 as brands restocked for year-end promotions
and remained at similar levels in 4Q25 despite seasonal softness as well as in 1Q26.
Industry utilization stayed broadly flat QoQ, at 80-85% in 2Q26, reflecting continued
supply discipline, followed by a slight uptick in 3Q26.
Over the medium to long term, we continue to believe the display industry is undergoing

structural change. Chinese panel makers have shifted their focus from top-line growth to
profitability, while lower government subsidies have reinforced supply discipline. We
believe investors increasingly recognize that the industry's production-to-order model can
remain sustainable, particularly as panel price cycles shortened to quarters in 2023-24 vs.
multiyear cycles in the previous decade. Consolidation actions, including LG Display's sale
of its Gen 8.5 Guangzhou fab to TCL and Sharp's closure of its Gen 10 Sakai fab, also

support a healthier supply backdrop (for more information, see Display – Structural
Changes on Supply Side Not Fairly Priced In, June 17, 2021).

Morgan Stanley Research 5
Risk/Reward Fair After Recent Correction
We view risk-reward as broadly balanced following the recent correction in panel stocks.
Below are our current views:
• AUO (2409.TW, Derrick Yang): We rate AUO Equal-weight with a PT of NT
$27.00, based on a 1.4x 2026e P/B multiple. While we believe the current round of
TV panel price increases is nearing an end, major panel makers should continue to
demonstrate solid supply discipline, providing downside support. We appreciate

AUO's efforts to diversify its business, but meaningful earnings contributions are
likely to take time.
• BOE (000725.SZ, Derrick Yang): We prefer BOE due to its scale advantage,
higher exposure to display and faster progress in glass core substrates. Our PT of
Rmb9.30 is based on 2.5x 2026e P/B, which we view as reasonable given our
estimated ROE of 5-8% over 2026-28 compared with BOE's average P/B of 1.1x and
ROE of 2-4% during 2023-25.
• Innolux (3481.TW, Derrick Yang): In semiconductors, our supply-chain checks

suggest that Innolux is participating in a foundry customer's glass core substrate
project. However, we do not expect meaningful contributions before 2028, and
additional competitors could enter as the industry moves toward mass production.
We maintain our Equal-weight rating and PT of NT$60.00, based on a 2.1x 2026e
P/B multiple.
• LG Display (034220.KS, Ryan Kim): Meaningful OLED revenue contribution
should increasingly improve earnings from 2H25, but potentially weaker end-

markets keep us from turning bullish on LGD. The stock trades at 0.6x 2026e P/B
vs. a historical mid-cycle level of 0.5x.
• TCL (000100.SZ, Derrick Yang): We are EW with a price target of Rmb4.70 (1.7x
2026e P/B). The stock is trading at 1.8x 2026e P/B vs. its mid-cycle average of 1.4x
since 2022.
• Greater China DDIC supply chain implications – Novatek (3034.TW, Daniel Yen):
Our Underweight thesis reflects weaker PC, smartphone and automotive demand,

gross margin pressure, and a lack of new growth drivers. That said, Novatek's
OLED DDI roadmap appears more competitive than those of its key Korean peers
in terms of both performance and cost, helping it gain share in Apple's iPhone
supply chain.

Where We Could Be Wrong
• Stronger end demand: If end demand for major applications turns out to be better
than expected, there could be stronger panel shipments and less panel price
pressure.
• More stringent output control: If major panel makers collectively adjust
utilization to an extreme extent, they could mitigate pricing pressure in the case of
softer demand.
• Non-commodity display business: If the non-commodity business progresses

faster than expected, panel makers could show better financial results.

Overweight (O). The stock's total return is expected to exceed the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next
12-18 months.
Equal-weight (E). The stock's total return is expected to be in line with the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over

the next 12-18 months.
Not-Rated (NR). Currently the analyst does not have adequate conviction about the stock's total return relative to the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage
universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next 12-18 months.
Underweight (U). The stock's total return is expected to be below the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next

12-18 months.

ABF substrates –  AT&S
announces expanded
collaboration with Marvell
Morgan Stanley Taiwan Limited+
Howard Kao
Equity Analyst
Howard.Kao@morganstanley.com                                                +886 2 2730-2989
Irene Yen
Equity Analyst
Irene.Yen@morganstanley.com                                                +886 2 2730-2869
Morgan Stanley Asia Limited+
Andy Meng, CFA
Equity Analyst

Andy.Meng@morganstanley.com                                                +852 2239-7689
Greater China Technology Hardware
Asia Pacific
Industry View In-Line
Details: AT&S (ATSV.VI, not covered) has expanded its IC substrate agreement with
Marvell (MRVL.O, covered by Joseph Moore) to support AI and cloud infrastructure
demand, confirming Marvell as the previously unnamed anchor customer behind the
Kulim expansion alongside AMD (report).
The build-out spans the Plant 2 fit-out and a new substrate core and advanced

communications with a subject company, public appearances
and trading securities held by a research analyst account.
Key Takeaways
AT&S' announcement of further collaboration with Marvell again implies strong
demand for advanced ABF substrates.
It should be viewed primarily as customer identification and confirmation of the
strategic relationship behind the June project...
...rather than adding another expansion on top of June’s €1.5-2.0bn plan.
We believe this implies that Marvell is buying priority access to the part of the AI

supply chain most likely to gate its shipments.
This supports our positive view on the ABF segment. We think it has positive
implications for Unimicron and Nan Ya PCB, both of which we rate OW.
September 23, 2026 11:24 AM GMT

Valuation Methodology and Risks
Unimicron (3037.TW)
Base case, residual income (RI) valuation model, which we think derives the most accurate
value of the firm given that it takes into account cost of equity. We use a cost of equity of 9.2%
[risk-free rate of 1% (10-year Taiwan government note yield), equity risk premium of 8.7%, and
a beta of 1.0], a medium-term growth rate of 15%, and a terminal growth rate of 3%.
Risks to Upside
n Better-than-expected ABF substrate demand from PC and server customers

n Capex cuts; halt to its capacity expansion plan
n Continued yield issues of alternative technology that doesn't require substrate (e.g.,
CoWoP)
Risks to Downside
n Sudden demand shortfall
n Technological change that would not require ABF substrates
n Intensifying competition
n Yield issues or production hiccups when ramping new capacity
Nan Ya PCB (8046.TW)
Base case, residual income (RI) valuation model, which we think derives the most accurate

value of the firm given that it takes into account cost of equity. We use a cost of equity of 9.3%
[risk-free rate of 1% (10-year Taiwan government note yield), equity risk premium of 8.7%, and
a beta of 1.0], a medium-term growth rate of 17%, and a terminal growth rate of 3%.
Risks to Upside
n Better-than-expected ABF and BT demand
n Faster-than-expected pickup in AI and 5G demand
n Stronger-than-expected ASP hike
n Continued yield issues of alternative technology that doesn't require substrate (e.g.

CoWoP)
Risks to Downside
n Sudden demand shortfall, creating headwinds for ABF substrate demand and pricing
n Technological change that would not require ABF substrates
n Intensifying competition

Analyst Stock Ratings
Overweight (O). The stock's total return is expected to exceed the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next
12-18 months.
Equal-weight (E). The stock's total return is expected to be in line with the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over

the next 12-18 months.
Not-Rated (NR). Currently the analyst does not have adequate conviction about the stock's total return relative to the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage
universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next 12-18 months.
Underweight (U). The stock's total return is expected to be below the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next

12-18 months.

大立光 (3008 TT) 公告 ，斥 資 新 台 幣 11.72 億 元 購 入 台 中 市 南 屯 區 約 2,259.25

第 7 度 購 買 不 動 產 ，7 筆 合 計 金 額 約 80.78 億 元 ， 目 的 皆 為 未 來 擴 充 產 能 需

展望 3Q26 ， 雖 然 iPhone18 標 準 版 手 機 鏡 頭 延 後 出 貨 ， 但 是 首 款 iPhone 摺
疊 機 開 賣 ， 以 及 可 變 光 圈 鏡 頭 較 傳 統7P 鏡 頭 漲 價 ， 皆 有 助 於 推 動 鏡 頭 旺 季

產 品 ， 又 因 增 加 多 個 檢 測 工 站 使 良 率 更 低 ， 毛 利 率 將 低 於2Q26 ， 預 估 稅 後
淨利 62.67 億 元 ， QoQ+34.19% ， EPS47.91 元 。

體 iPhone 銷 量 持 平 ；iPhone 半 導 體 零 組 件 多 為 自 製 ，iPhone 抵 抗 成 本 上 揚
能力優於 Android 手 機，故 能 依 照 原 定 計 畫 升 級 高 階 機 種 主 鏡 頭 為 可 變 光 圈

導 致 良 率 下 降，因 此 鏡 頭 價 格 較 傳 統 7P 鏡 頭 更 高，預 估 2026 年營收 653.47

3 群益投顧 
  【 投 資 評 等 說 明 】 
  評等  定義  
  強力買進 (Strong Buy)  首 次 評 等 潛 在 上 漲 空 間≥ 35%  
  買進 (Buy)  15%≤ 首 次 評 等 潛 在 上 漲 空 間<35%  
  區間操作 (Trading Buy)  5%≤ 首 次 評 等 潛 在 上 漲 空 間<15%

中立 (Neutral)  
無 法 由 基 本 面 給 予 投 資 評 等 
預 期 近 期 股 價 將 處 於 盤 整 
建 議 降 低 持 股

【 投 資 評 等 調 整 機 制 】 
  投 資 評 等 係 「 首 次 」 給 予 特 定 個 股 投 資 評 等 時 ， 其 前 一 日 收 盤 價 相 較3 個
月目標價之潛在上漲空間計算而得。個股投資評等分為 四 個等級，定義如
上 。 爾 後 的 投 資 評 等係 依 循 「 首 次 評 等 」 ， 直 到 停 止 推 薦 。  
「 強 力 買 進 」、「 買 進 」及「 區 間 操 作 」均有 upside 目 標 價 。 差 別 僅 在 於 ，
首 次 評 等 時 潛 在 報 酬 率 不 同 。 「 中 立 」 則 無 目 標 價 。 
一旦我們給予特定個股「強力買進」 、 「買進」 或「區間操作」 之投資評
等，就是責任的開始，爾後將透過各式研究報告作定期性、持續性追蹤基
本 面 及 股 價 變 化 ， 直 到 停 止 推 薦 。 
停 止 推 薦 情 境 ： 
1.  達 目 標 價 。 
2.  雖 未 達 原 訂 目 標 價 ， 但 檢 視 基 本 面 、 訊 息 面 、 籌 碼 面 等 多 方 訊 息 ，
研 判 股 價 上 漲 空 間 已 然 有 限 ， 將 適 時 出 具 降 評 報 告 。 
3.  推 薦 後 股 價 不 漲 反 跌 ， 亦 將 出 具 降 評 報 告 。

【免責聲明】  
  本研究報告僅提供予特定人之客戶作為參考資料「非經同意不得轉載」。
我們並不確保此資訊的完整性與正確性，投資人應了解，報告中有關未來
預測之陳述可能不會實現，因而不應被依賴。而且此報告並非根據特定投
資 目 的 或 依 預 定 對 象 之 財 務 狀 況 所 撰 寫 出 來 的，因 此，此 研 究 報 告 的 目 的 ，
既非對投資人於買賣證券、選擇權、期貨或其他證券相關之衍生性商品提
供詢價服務，亦非作為進行交易的要約。投資人應注意到相關證券之價值
及收益，可能會有無預警地上升或下降，產生投資回報金額可能比原始投
資 來 得 少 的 情 形 。

### Page 2

2

雙鴻為台灣散熱模組廠商，主要提供風扇、散熱片、熱導管等設計組合而成散熱工
具，裝置在筆記型電腦、桌上型電腦、伺服器及智慧型手機等產品。高速運算晶片
發熱量持續增加， 散熱管理重要性提升。 散熱管理技術過往以主被動混合式熱管理
方案(鰭片+風扇)為主 ， 近年主流設計為均熱板 、 熱導管及3DVC 的散熱解決方案 ，
伺服器應用客戶積極導入水冷式散熱解決方案，六大關鍵零組件包含 Cold Plate、
CDU(Cooling Distribution Units)、Rack、RDHx、Quick Connectors、Manifold。 
雙鴻生產基地位於泰國、中國廣州、昆山、重慶、合肥。台灣散熱模組廠主要競爭
對手為奇鋐、Cooler Master、台達電、超眾及力致等等。客戶包括國內外筆電品
牌大廠及台灣 ODM 代工廠。2Q26 產品組合：PC 17%，VGA 4%，Server 78%，
Others 1%。 
水冷營收比重持續提高：先前雙鴻公告 7 月自結獲利，單月營收 37.7 億元，稅前
淨利 8.3 億元，稅後淨利 6.0 億元，稅後 EPS 6.47 元，優於預期，主因 7 月認列
部份 6 月遞延營收。8 月份客戶拉貨波動，單月營收月減 16.6%，預期 9 月份將
會回升。3Q26 雙鴻 GB300 水冷板、Manifold 出貨增加，以及預期 9 月份 AWS 
Trainium3 及輝達 Vera Rubin 世代相關水冷產品開始出貨，逐漸增加貢獻，主要
貢獻將落在 4Q26。 
研究部推估雙鴻 3Q26、4Q26 水冷營收比重達 61％、63%。營收分別為 103 億、
109 億元。水冷營收比重增加，同時增強獲利率表現，預估毛利率分別為29.9%、
30.3%，稅後 EPS 16.77 元、17.14 元。 
認證輝達 Vera Rubin 水冷板中 ：雙鴻目前正在驗證輝達 Vera Rubin 世代水冷板 ，
預計最快 9 月底通過驗證。研究部認為短期雙鴻出貨 Vera Rubin 世代相關水冷產
品將先以 Manifold 為主，待驗證完成後進一步加入營收獲利貢獻預估。同時雙鴻
也有望延續進入 Vera Rubin Ultra 專案，待後續相關水冷產品開發。 
ASIC 方面，雙鴻將量產 AWS Trainium3 水冷相關產品包含水冷板、 Inner 
Manifold、Rack Manifold，惟 4Q26 主要為小量產階段，預期主要貢獻放量將落
在 2027 年。後續包含 Meta ASIC 及 CDU 產品都有望額外增添貢獻雙鴻水冷營
收。 
產能持續擴充 ， 主要受惠水冷市場產值擴大 ：公司積極拓展伺服器水冷散熱市場機
會，2026 年、2027 年持續增加伺服器水冷產品產能。目前水冷板月產能包含廣州
及泰國共 400k pcs， 後續視情況在泰國增加100k~200k pcs。Manifold 台灣 2k、
泰國 3k。隨著 AI 伺服器散熱需求越來越高，不論 GPU、ASIC 散熱設計都越趨複
雜，如無塵室等級要求提高，也加大投資需求，對獲利率表現都會形成挑戰。 
水冷散熱供應者眾，目前水冷散熱零組件市場以奇鋐及 Cooler Master 產能較大
及佔據主要份額。雙鴻營運主要能受惠整體水冷散熱滲透率、市場產值提升，帶動
營收規模擴大及獲利金額成長。預估雙鴻 2026 年、2027 年水冷散熱營收比重
59%、68%。2026 年營收 385 億元，年增 65%，毛利率 29.6%，營益率 17.8%，
稅後 EPS 56.93 元。2027 年營收 513 億元，年增33%，毛利率 18.6%，稅後 EPS 
79.87 元。

新日興 (3376 TT)  Trading Buy

低軌道衛星、 AI 伺服器水冷散熱零組件為未來成長動能。  
投資建議 ：折疊式螢幕手機 Hinge 於 2H26 有獲利貢獻， AI 伺
服器水冷散熱零組件 2027 年將有營收挹注 ， 投資評等為Trading 
Buy ，目標價為 203 元。  
預估 NB Hinge 2026 年營收與 2025 年持平： 營運重心原以某美
系客戶產品為主，故於 NB Hinge 市佔率逐年下滑。受需求不佳
影響， NB Hinge 2025 年營收 YoY+5.1% 。為分散營運風險，公
司積極爭取其他 NB 品牌訂單，但受 NB 市況不佳影響，預估
2026 年 NB Hinge 營收與 2025 年持平。  
穿戴式產品預估 2026 年營收 YoY-17.6% ：穿戴式產品包含第
二代一般型充電盒 Hinge 、高階版 TWS 充電盒 Hinge 、耳罩式
耳機 Hinge 等。因 2024 年基期較高， 2025 年穿戴式產品營收
YoY-28.8% 。受消費市場不佳影響，預估 2026 年穿戴式產品營
收 YoY-17.6% 。  
折疊式螢幕手機 Hinge 於 2H26 有獲利貢獻： 新日興於折疊螢
幕式產品 Hinge 與美系客戶已開發多年，此美系客戶已於 3Q26
發布其首款折疊式螢幕手機，預估折疊式螢幕手機 Hinge 於
2H26 年有獲利貢獻，但較預期為低 。 
預期 AI 伺服器水冷散熱零組件 2027 年將有營收挹注： 新日興
的精密加工設備主要在台灣，近年開拓精密零件領域業務，已
取得低軌道衛星零件、電動自行車精密零件、光學檢測儀器零
件、模治具零件等訂單，營收逐年提升中。低軌道衛星零件已
量產出貨，取得品項亦逐步增加中。  
新日興有 CNC 加工、雷射焊接、雷射切割多年製造經驗，亦積
極切入 AI 伺服器水冷散熱領域。已與多家客戶洽談分歧管代工
業務，目前產品認證中，預期 4Q26 有機會少量出貨 ， 2027 年
有較顯著營收貢獻 ，未來將爭取快速接頭代工訂單 。

6 群益投顧 
  【投資評等說明】  
  評等  定義  
  強力買進 (Strong Buy)  首次評等潛在上漲空間 ≥ 35%  
  買進 (Buy)  15% ≤首次評等潛在上漲空間 <35%  
  區間操作 (Trading Buy) 5% ≤首次評等潛在上漲空間 <15%

中立 (Neutral)  
無法由基本面給予投資評等  
預期近期股價將處於盤整  
建議降低持股

【投資評等調整機制】  
  投資評等係「首次」給予特定個股投資評等時，其前一日收盤價相較 3 個月
目標價之潛在上漲空間計算而得。個股投資評等分為四個等級，定義如上。
爾後的投資評等係依循「首次評等」，直到停止推薦。   
「強力買進」、「買進」及「區間操作」均有 upside 目標價。差別僅在於，
首次評等時潛在報酬率不同。「中立」則無目標價。  
一旦我們給予特定個股「強力買進」 、 「買進」或「區間操作」之投資評等，
就是責任的開始，爾後將透過各式研究報告作定期性、持續性追蹤基本面及
股價變化，直到停止推薦。  
停止推薦情境：  
1.  達目標價。  
2.  雖未達原訂目標價，但檢視基本面、訊息面、籌碼面等多方訊息，研
判股價上漲空間已然有限，將適時出具降評報告。  
3.  推薦後股價不漲反跌。

【免責聲明】  
  本研究報告僅提供予特定人之客戶作為參考資料「非經同意不得轉載」 。我
們並不確保此資訊的完整性與正確性，投資人應了解，報告中有關未來預測
之陳述可能不會實現，因而不應被依賴。而且此報告並非根據特定投資目的
或依預定對象之財務狀況所撰寫出來的，因此，此研究報告的目的，既非對
投資人於買賣證券、選擇權、期貨或其他證券相關之衍生性商品提供詢價服
務，亦非作為進行交易的要約。投資人應注意到相關證券之價值及收益，可
能會有無預警地上升或下降，產生投資回報金額可能比原始投資來得少的
情形。

3Q26 營收及獲利表現強勁 
3Q26 進入旺季，板卡業務復甦，Server 料源轉好，遞延訂單開始出貨，估
營收季增 55%至 156億元，年增 34%。低毛利率 AI Server出貨較多，估毛
利率季減 3百分點至 17%，營業利益 15.3億元，季增 66%，年增 145%。
估稅後 7億元，季增 93%，年增 31%，EPS 5.7元，比原先預估上修 19%，
主因高毛利率一般型 Server 比重上升及 PC 相關產品(MB、VGA)業績谷底
翻揚，造成毛利率及本業獲利比原先預期佳。 
記憶體大漲，但客戶殺價情況減緩，反而有助整體毛利率上升 
公司終端產品漲價減低記憶體大漲影響，客戶殺價情況亦減緩，有助整體毛
利率上升，1Q/2Q26毛利率 15%/20%，遠比 2025年 13.6%佳。下半年 AI 
Server料源逐漸改善，占比上升，估華擎 3Q/4Q26降至 17.0%/15.8%，但
全年毛利率 16.7%，年增 3.1百分點。2027年受 AI Server GB系列開始出
貨，毛利率降至 15.5%，年減 1.2百分點，但營收規模擴大，費用率下滑，
估 2026/27年營業利益率 8.9%/8.3%，比 2025年 5.7%佳。 
2026/27 年營收及獲利維持 20%以上高成長 
2026/27年受惠資料中心建置加快，企業端推論需求提高，估一般型 Server
營收成長 73%/18%。2026/27 年北美、亞洲等 新客戶訂單增加， 估 AI 
Server 營收成長 57%/43%(占整體營收比重 51.1%/56.7%)。合計 2026/27
年整體 Server營收(一般型+AI)年增 61%/37%，占比 70%/74%。 
合計華擎 2026/27年營收年增 20%/29%至 574/743億元(2026年下修 4%，
主因 AI Server 缺料)，估 2026/27 年毛利率 16.7%/15.5%，比 2025 年
13.55%改善。合計稅後 23.5/29.5億元，年增 24%/26%，EPS 1 8.98/23.87
元，比先前預估略下修 1%/1%，主因少數股權項目扣除變多 。受惠 AI 
Server需求高，工業電腦明顯復甦，華擎獲利表現仍佳，維持買進評等。 
元大觀點 
⧫  
3Q26 進入旺季，板卡業務復甦， Server 料源轉好，遞延訂單開始出
貨，估營收季增 55%至 156 億元，年增 34%。 
⧫  
記憶體大漲， 但客戶殺價情況減緩， 反而 有助整體毛利率上升 ，估
2026/27 年毛利率 16.7%/15.5%，比 2025 年 13.6%上升。 
⧫  
AI Server 及 IPC 需求高，毛利率上升，獲利表現佳，維持買進評等。
目標價 280 元係以本益比 12 倍、2H26~1H27 EPS 23.55 元推得。

營運分析
3Q26 營收及獲利表現強勁
2Q26受 Server的 CPU缺貨影響，營收季減 24%至 101億元，年減 16%，但 AI Server 訂單仍強
勁。3Q26 進入旺季，板卡業務復甦， Server 料源轉好，遞延訂單開始出貨，估營收季增 55%至
156億元，年增 34%。低毛利率 AI Server 出貨較多，估毛利率季減 3百分點至 17%，營業利益
15.3億元，季增 66%，年增 145%。業外在利息收入及其他收入挹注下，估獲利 0.4億元。合計稅
後 7 億元，季增 93%，年增 31%，EPS 5.7 元，比原先預估上修 19%，主因高毛利率一般型
Server 比重上升及 PC 相關產品(MB、VGA)業績谷底翻揚，造成毛利率及本業獲利比原先預期佳。

4Q26 進入最旺季，板卡業務持續復甦， Server 需求暢旺，估營收季增 17%至 183 億元，年增
34%。低毛利率 AI Server  GB開始出貨，估毛利率季減 1.2百分點至 15.8%，營業利益 16.9億元，
季增 11%，年增 120%。業外在利息收入及其他收入挹注下，估獲利 0.4億元。合計稅後 7.64億
元，季增 8%，年增 54%，EPS 6.19元，獲利穩定向上。

記憶體短缺且價格大漲，客戶殺價情況亦減緩，反而有助整體毛利率上升 
1Q26記憶體大漲，華擎與客戶合作因應，VGA/Server相關產品向客戶動態報價，客戶自行採買更
便宜記憶體或減少記憶體配置量，降低影響； IPC 則因記憶體配備無法輕易變動，較難如 Server
採減少配置作法，對價格敏感的客戶會遞延拉貨。需求部分，MB 出貨雖未配備 DRAM，但終端產
品漲價，消費性電子客戶較難適應，出貨下滑；其餘產品銷售亦受波及，但比 MB影響略小。 
公司終端產品漲價減低記憶體大漲影響， 且記憶體、 CPU、GPU 料源不足，造成低毛利率 AI 
Server出貨不順，客戶殺價情況亦減緩，反而有助整體毛利率上升，1Q/2Q26毛利率 15%/20%，
遠比 2025 年 13.6%佳。下半年 AI Server 料源逐漸改善，占比上升，因此估華擎 3Q/4Q26 降至
17.0%/15.8%，但全年毛利率 16.7%，年增 3.1百分點。2027年受 AI Server GB系列開始出貨，
毛利率降至 15.5%，年減 1.2 百分點，但營收規模擴大，費用率下滑，估 2026/27 年營業利益率
8.9%/8.3%，遠比 2025年 5.7%佳。

資料中心建置加速，Server 銷售樂觀 
2026/27 年受惠資料中心建置加快，企業端推論需求提高，一般型 Server 出貨暢旺，估營收成長
73%/18%。AI Server方面，2026/27年北美、亞洲等新客戶訂單增加，估 AI Server營收持續成長
57%/43%(占整體營收比重 51.1%/56.7%)。AI Server 一台單價高達 30~40萬美金，但大部分關鍵
零組件如： GPU、CPU、DRAM 等均外購，毛利率偏低，對毛利率走勢略為不利影響。 合計
2026/27年整體 Server營收(一般型+AI)年增 61%/37%，占比 70%/74%。 
圖 5：華擎 Server 營收成長顯著

資料來源：元大投顧預估 
2026/27 年營收及獲利維持 20%以上高成長 
1)工業電腦產業龍頭研華 B/B ratio 下半年維持在 1.4~1.5高檔，景氣復甦確立，邊緣 AI成為趨勢，
2025年成長 30%，2026/27年受惠一些專案陸續出貨(主要增加北美串流服務商大單)，成長加快至
81%/18%。 
2)MB/VGA從 2025年下半年記憶體大漲，銷售開始受影響，估 2026年營收分別衰退 39%/30%，
2027年上游原物料漲價趨緩，加上 AMD及 Intel有新品推出，估成長 7%/14%。 
合計華擎 2026/27年預估營收年增 20%/29%至 574/743億元(2026下修 4%，主因 AI Server缺料)，
記憶體大漲，客戶殺價情況亦減緩，反而有助整體毛利率上升 ，估華擎 2026/27 年毛利率
16.7%/15.5%，比 2025 年 13.55%改善。合計稅後 23.5/29.5 億元，年增 24%/26%，EPS 
18.98/23.87元，比先前預估略下修 1%/1%，主因少數股權項目扣除變多。

產業概況  
2026 年 PC 出貨恐衰退 6.3% 
受到上游記憶體成本上揚，PC廠商即使轉嫁或降低規格，均將影響消費者購買意願，因此將 2026
年 PC (NB+DT)出貨量下調至衰退 6.3%，NB亦下修至衰退 5.8%，產品項目中電競 NB成長 1.4%，
仍維持成長(其餘產品均衰退)，主因電競 NB具剛性需求，目前在 NB滲透率 15%仍低。華擎在電
競產品含：主機板、繪圖卡等，比重約 25%，在 PC不景氣時，銷售具有支撐。

圖 9：全球電競 NB 出貨量預估

資料來源：IDC、元大投顧預估 
AI、ASIC、通用型強勢出擊，2026 年美系 CSP 資本支出估年增 91%  
在 ChatGPT 等 AI 應用陸續推向市場，各大業者紛紛開始研發自有超級大模型，包括 Gemini 
(Google)、Claude (Anthropic)、Llama (Meta) 等，各大品牌開始大舉投入大型語言模型(LLM)市場，
且每一個產品的智慧皆持續提高，部分消費者也陸續從 ChatGPT 陣營轉移至 Gemini 陣營，反映
出消費者開始逐漸提升對 AI的黏著度。根據 Grand View Research 調查，2024 年全球 AI 市場營
收預估約 2,792 億美元，預估 2030 年市場規模超過 3 兆美元，擁有超過 30% 的年複合增長率。 
面對這爆發性的長期成長趨勢，CSP業者(Amazon、Microsoft、Google、Meta)在法說會上一致強
調，AI投資已轉變為一項橫跨 2026 年的結構性戰略，CSP大廠不僅持續擴大對 GB300等次世代
AI 伺服器的採購，更將重點放在資料中心基礎設施的長期戰略規劃，以應對 AI 運算對電力及散熱
系統強勁成長的需求，確保未來數年內擁有足夠的能源與容量來支持持續迭代的大模型部署。本中
心認為，2026年美國四大 CSP資本支出將年增 91%，且將有一半的成長來自於資料中心建置，代
表了資料中心的不足及未來伺服器需求。明年不僅僅是 NVIDIA GB300 的天下，AWS、Google、
Meta ASIC的崛起也將是一大關鍵，其中又以 Google TPU需求最為強勁，已經有兩個客戶預計將
採購 TPU。 
另外，受惠於 AI訓練與推論需求爆發的連帶效應，本中心預估 2026年通用型伺服器出貨量將年增
23%，其中以存儲型伺服器需求最為強勁。隨著生成式 AI 應用普及和使用者數量暴增，CSP 等業
者必須不斷擴充容量，且不僅限於高階 GPU 伺服器，龐大的 AI模型訓練和推論在使用狀態中將消
耗大量的數據(DATA)，使得存儲型伺服器的需求大增。

公司簡介  
華擎成立於 2002年 5月，原為華碩子公司，以銷售中、低階主機板為主，後跨入工業電腦、伺服器等領域。後來華碩、和
碩分割後，華擎成為和碩子公司。產品組合(2025年)：主機板 20%、工業電腦 4%、一般伺服器 13%、AI伺服器 39%、其
他 24%。旗下設二家子公司，分別為永擎(持股 60%；主攻伺服器)、東擎(持股 64%；主打工業電腦)。華擎未設工廠，產
品主要交由和碩及陸商(中國、越南設廠)代工。公司未來發展以非 PC產品為主，有助分散營運風險。

ESG 分析  
分別藉由「在 ESG議題上的曝險」和「個別公司在 ESG議題上的執行力」兩個面向來衡量公司於 ESG上的表現。 
► ESG 總分： 華擎整體的 ESG風險評級屬於中風險，於 Sustainalytics資料庫所覆蓋的公司中排名位於中間位置，在科
技硬體行業的公司中排名則略為落後同業。 
► 在 ESG 議題上的曝險： 華擎的整體曝險屬於低水準，且略優於科技硬體行業的平均水準。公司較需要改善的  ESG 議
題包含商業道德、人力資源和公司的數據安全等。 
► 個別公司在 ESG 議題上的執行力：華擎在針對重大 ESG議題的管理水準和執行力屬中等，已採取若干措施來管理與實
質 ESG議題相關的風險，公司擁有完整對 ESG的揭露，包含成立永續發展辦公室及發布 CSR報告書等，展現了對企
業社會責任的實踐。但在關鍵領域如職場多元性、供應鏈管理仍缺乏相應的政策與計畫。儘管如此，該公司並未捲入具
有重大財務影響的風險事件。

產能滿載且供不應求，漲價效應有望延續至 2028 年；(3) 新產能
將於 2Q27 陸續開出，帶動營收與獲利持續跳升等因素，投資評

2 群益投顧 
  ESG(Environment, Social, Governance) ：  
信昌電 (6173 TT ）秉持永續發展核心理念，將 ESG 願景融入公司治理與日
常營運，建構完善的組織架構與管理機制。公司設立永續發展委員會，全面
推動環境、社會與治理各項策略，確保永續資訊的透明度與合規性。在公司
治理與風險管理層面，信昌電致力於落實誠信經營，落實嚴謹的供應商行為
準則與廉潔承諾，並結合國際品質與管理系統認證（如 ISO 9001 、 IATF 
16949 、 IECQ QC080000 、 ISO 45001 等），持續精進營運體質。在環境保護
與綠色營運上，公司以介電陶瓷粉末研發與 MLCC 製造為核心，落實溫室
氣體盤查與廢棄物、水資源管理，並積極投資博德新能與博新能源，分階段
布局再生能源與儲能設備以邁向 RE100 目標。在社會共融與人才發展方面，
公司提供完善的薪酬福利、多元教育訓練與健康檢查，積極維護職場安全衛
生，同時透過華科事業群慈善基金會等機構長期投入聽覺照顧、偏鄉教育與
弱勢關懷等公益行動，展現企業公民價值。

公司簡介：  
信昌電 (6173 TT) 成立於 1990 年，並於 2002 年 4 月上櫃。公司隸屬於華新
麗華集團，母公司為華新科技，持股比例約為 43.1% 。信昌電為台灣少數具
備從上游介電陶瓷粉末到下游被動元件垂直整合能力的廠商。品牌為 PDC，
主要產品包括 MLCC 、 Chip-R 及介電陶瓷粉末。生產基地方面，台灣桃園
廠生產 Powder 及 R- Chip ，楊梅一廠主要生產 MLCC ，另建置楊梅二廠 (今
年投資 15 億，主要生產高壓 /低損耗，高溫穩定型  MLCC ）及六甲廠（去年
Capex 12 億投資粉末場，主要建置新一代自動化高效生產陶瓷粉末及開發
次世代粉材），主要產品包含：介電陶瓷粉末、晶片電容器 (MLCC) 、晶片
電阻器與電感產品。 2026 年上半年產品組合佔比為： MLCC 佔 68% 、晶片
電阻佔 16% 、介電陶瓷粉末佔 12% 、電感佔 2%及其他佔 2%。

信昌電現金減資 6%、 10/7 起暫停交易、 10/19 新股上櫃：

能力，擬辦理現金減資退還股本予股東，預計減資比率約為 6％，每股返還

約 60 股（即每仟股換發約 940 股）及退還現金約新台幣 600 元。舊股票將
於 10/7~10/16 號暫停交易，新股於 10/19 號換發上櫃買賣。

現爆發性成長，預估 MLCC 總產值 VR200 較 GB300 增長 150% 以上。其中，
具備防板彎與高耐壓特性的 Mega Cap （單價為一般產品 6~8 倍以上）以及
高穩定度的 NP0 產品出貨將顯著放量，上述產品毛利率顯著高於平均毛利
率，加上信昌電目前高階 MLCC 產能呈現滿載，公司表示 2H26 有望再度調
漲售價， 2026 年全年漲幅將達 30%( 上半年已漲 10~15%) ，預估信昌電 2H26

等新一代高壓（ 800V HVDC ）與高功率架構演進以及下一世代的 Feynman ，
系統對高階大尺寸被動元件的需求呈現爆發性成長。目前高階 MLCC 產能
持續緊缺，廠區產能利用率呈現滿載，在供不應求的市況下，有望推升
MLCC 持續調漲價格。由於 Mega Cap 以及 NP0 MLCC 的需求遠大於現有
供給，高階產能持續處於結構性緊缺狀態，研究部預估供不應求的狀況有望
延續至 2028 年。

目前信昌電高階 MLCC 產能呈現滿載，為因應強勁的市場需求，信昌電積
極擴產佈局，規劃中的楊梅二廠與六甲新廠均預計於 2027 年第二季完工、
下半年逐步放量。其中，楊梅二廠將專注生產高壓、低損耗及高溫穩定型
MLCC，而六甲新廠則負責建置新一代自動化高效陶瓷粉末與次世代粉材產
線。雙新廠的落成不僅能有效緩解高階產品的供給壓力，更透過粉末研發到
元件製造的上下游垂直整合，進一步優化成本結構、推升產品毛利率。綜上
所述，在新產能開出及漲價效應雙重利多發酵下，預估信昌電 2027 年營收
為 94.72 億元 (YOY+64.2%) ，因 AI 比重顯著拉升 ， 帶動毛利率拉升至 35.20% ，
2027 年稅後 EPS 12.93 元，獲利將進一步拉升。

投資建議：  
考量因新一世代 AI 伺服器的電源瓦數及峰值電壓持續攀升，將帶動高階
MLCC 規格及用量需求持續提升，預估 2027 年將會更加吃緊，基於產業供
需狀況強勁，投資評等為 Buy ，以 2H27~1H28 稅後減資後稀釋 EPS 為計算
基礎，給予 24XPER ，目標價 403 元。

【投資評等調整機制】  
  投資評等係「首次」給予特定個股投資評等時，其前一日收盤價相較 3 個月
目標價之潛在上漲空間計算而得。個股投資評等分為四個等級，定義如上。
爾後的投資評等係依循「首次評等」，直到停止推薦。   
「強力買進」、「買進」及「區間操作」均有 upside 目標價。差別僅在於，
首次評等時潛在報酬率不同。「中立」則無目標價。  
一旦我們給予特定個股「強力買進」 、 「買進」或「區間操作」之投資評等，
就是責任的開始，爾後將透過各式研究報告作定期性、持續性追蹤基本面及
股價變化，直到停止推薦。  
停止推薦情境：  
1.  達目標價。  
2.  雖未達原訂目標價，但檢視基本面、訊息面、籌碼面等多方訊息，研
判股價上漲空間已然有限，將適時出具降評報告。  
3.  推薦後股價不漲反跌。

【免責聲明】  
  本研究報告僅提供予特定人之客戶作為參考資料「非經同意不得轉載」 。我
們並不確保此資訊的完整性與正確性，投資人應了解，報告中有關未來預測
之陳述可能不會實現，因而不應被依賴。而且此報告並非根據特定投資目的
或依預定對象之財務狀況所撰寫出來的，因此，此研究報告的目的，既非對
投資人於買賣證券、選擇權、期貨或其他證券相關之衍生性商品提供詢價服
務，亦非作為進行交易的要約。投資人應注意到相關證券之價值及收益，可
能會有無預警地上升或下降，產生投資回報金額可能比原始投資來得少的
情形。

矽格 (6257 TT)  Buy

AI 和矽光訂單貢獻將逐步增加，建議 Buy。  
投資建議 ： AI、 ASIC 、矽光子與高速運算是矽格 2026 年最明
確、也是最重要的成長引擎。受惠於客戶端龐大的需求，這三
大板塊的營收佔比已躍升至 20% 以上。其中， ASIC 與矽光子是
目前毛利率最高的產品線，加上 CP 佔比提升，產品組合改變，
有利毛利率向上。預估矽格 2026 年稅後 EPS 9.91 元。雖消費
性電子需求溫和，不過矽格積極開發新客戶、新產品以增加成
長動能。美系 CSP 持續增加 ASIC 量，帶動後段測試需求吃緊，
除美國外，矽格還有日本及歐美 ASIC 等新客戶，另原大客戶也
跨入 AI 晶片，公司配合增加資本支出，將帶動未來 AI 相關訂
單成長 。 由於測試產能吃緊(測試廠 80% 為滿載 ， 考慮換線時間)，
預期價格將續漲，加上新產能開出， 2026 年營收和毛利率有望
逐季向上，因此建議 Buy ，目標價為 304 元 (2027 年 PER24X) 。 
2Q26 稅後 EPS 2.52 元 ：矽格 2Q26 營收 58.81 億元，
QoQ+11.09% 。 2Q26 雖然部份客戶產品受到記憶體價格上漲影
響，對營收成長動能造成一定程度壓抑；惟受惠客戶在 AI 伺服
器、 ASIC 、AI Connectivity 、矽光子、網通晶片及記憶體等領域
需求持續擴增，加上公司擴產計畫穩步推進，先前追加資本支
出所採購之設備將陸續到位，並逐步挹注營收表現，使營收持
續保持一定動能。受惠稼動率維持高檔，使毛利率也上揚。矽
格 2Q26 稅後 EPS 2.52 元。  
2026 年資本支出提升至 88 億元 ：矽格董事會上修全年度資本
支出，由原先規劃的 59 億元大幅提高至 88 億元，增幅達 49%。
主要用於採購先進製程測試設備，以滿足 AI、 ASIC 及 HPC 等
強勁的市場需求。預計 2H26 湖口二廠將加入生產。因獲得客戶
訂單保證，將在 07/2026 開始貢獻營收，以矽光為主；規模較大
中興三廠亦提前於 4Q26 建置完畢，為中長期先進製程訂單提
供充裕的產能擴展空間，預計 1Q27 進入量產。折舊費用方面，
新設備 4Q25 陸續安裝， 2Q26 後，折舊費用將會逐季增加。

2 群益投顧 
  矽格 ESG ：  
矽格體認企業永續經營運作與全球多元劇變之發展密不可分，因此我們建
立並持續發展各項符合國際倡議之永續經營管理策略，善盡企業社會責任，
共同保護我們所共享的地球環境。  
「落實公司治理」  
氣候相關財務揭露  (TCFD) 報告，揭露透過治理、策略、風險管理、指標與
目標，並於同年成立風險管理委員會展開氣候變遷調適及減緩管理行動，董
事會亦每季審查集團各子公司之溫室氣體推展進度及成效管理，邁向低碳
永續之倡議。  
「環境保護永續」  
矽格積極實施低碳策略之行動方案，落實節能、節水、減廢等相關作為邁進
永續封測，並積極佈局支持再生能源使用。  
「智慧創新管理」  
持續推動智慧製造工廠，落實運用智慧管理模式提升客戶滿意績效的最佳
化表現。自主研發機台因應不同客戶客製化需求產出所需，提供客戶多樣化
選擇和更具競爭力的解決方案優化複雜製程，以低碳產品之前瞻技術為永
續競爭力。  
「綠色營運供應」  
綠色營運供應落實管理，矽格不僅關心企業內部的環境管理及相關教育訓
練，同時也關注供應商管理，推動供應商共同承擔環境及社會責任。因此，
矽格建立供應商管理程序，確保企業永續發展落實執行與督導供應鏈。  
「建立友善職場」  
落實勞動人權策略提供多元溝通管道途徑，在符合法令、公平與合理性之前
提下，致力符合同仁期待與需求，提升全體同仁勞動權益，促使職場達到溝
通無障礙。  
「投入社會參與」  
投入社會參與落實企業社會責任議題是矽格集團持續並強化落實的永續發
展策略之一，不論是贊助醫學預防的臺大醫院之 「心臟血管基因研究計畫」 、
落實在地關懷世光教養院附設拙茁家園車輛贊助等 … 都是矽格依循永續理
念，秉持踏實精神與環境、社會共生共榮的態度在企業永續的道路上堅定前
行。

【投資評等調整機制】  
  投資評等係「首次」給予特定個股投資評等時，其前一日收盤價相較 3 個月
目標價之潛在上漲空間計算而得。個股投資評等分為四個等級，定義如上。
爾後的投資評等係依循「首次評等」，直到停止推薦。   
「強力買進」、「買進」及「區間操作」均有 upside 目標價。差別僅在於，
首次評等時潛在報酬率不同。「中立」則無目標價。  
一旦我們給予特定個股「強力買進」 、 「買進」或「區間操作」之投資評等，
就是責任的開始，爾後將透過各式研究報告作定期性、持續性追蹤基本面及
股價變化，直到停止推薦。  
停止推薦情境：  
1.  達目標價。  
2.  雖未達原訂目標價，但檢視基本面、訊息面、籌碼面等多方訊息，研
判股價上漲空間已然有限，將適時出具降評報告。  
3.  推薦後股價不漲反跌。

【免責聲明】  
  本研究報告僅提供予特定人之客戶作為參考資料「非經同意不得轉載」 。我
們並不確保此資訊的完整性與正確性，投資人應了解，報告中有關未來預測
之陳述可能不會實現，因而不應被依賴。而且此報告並非根據特定投資目的
或依預定對象之財務狀況所撰寫出來的，因此，此研究報告的目的，既非對
投資人於買賣證券、選擇權、期貨或其他證券相關之衍生性商品提供詢價服
務，亦非作為進行交易的要約。投資人應注意到相關證券之價值及收益，可
能會有無預警地上升或下降，產生投資回報金額可能比原始投資來得少的
情形。

晶心科(6533.TT) 
產業：電子–半導體 
組織調整完畢，靜待成效展現 
 投資評價與建議 
隨著RISC-V需求持續提升，公司開案數同步增加，惟公司短期仍以授權費為
主，且轉向大型客戶使得案件認列時程拉⻑，營收波動也較大。 
 重點評論分析 
3Q26尚無客戶大型專案貢獻，推估營收季減約18%，4Q26將回復成⻑：來自
歐美車用客戶也開始貢獻授權金 ， 惟美系CSP客戶因大型專案墊高2Q26基期 ，
推估25Q3營收4.64億元，QoQ-18.1%，因人員裁撤，費用將明顯下滑，推估
約4.5億元，本業有望轉為正數，EPS 0.25元。展望4Q26，因季底通常為授權
金認列高峰，推估營收5.15億元，QoQ+11.5%，本業亦有望維持獲利。 
費用開始嚴控，有望自2H26起維持本業獲利態勢，2027年展望正向：隨著公
司轉向大型客戶專案與車用市場，因案件時程拉⻑和車用認證期較⻑，使得各
季的營收波動較大，展望未來，隨著歐美客戶車用產品開案完成，車用產品將
是主要成⻑動能，惟目前仍以授權費為主，雖消費性產品需求不佳，然在客戶
降低成本考量，以及網通產品為提升運算與資料傳輸的效能與彈性，如達發
(6526)已宣布擴大採用RISC-V ， 皆有助公司營運 ， 而費用自3Q26起開始嚴控 ，
本業有望開始維持獲利，2027年隨著案件數進⼀步增加，本業獲利將明顯提
升；整體而言，公司對於RISC-V未來發展趨勢仍樂觀看待。 
 投資風險 
先進製程等案件持續不如預期。

| 公司簡介  
晶心科為全球RISC-V CPU IP龍頭廠，市占率約30%：公司成立於2005年，早期專注自有架構V3，2016年開始轉
為RISC-V架構之CPU IP授權 ， 目前授權費占比約65%為主要營收貢獻 ， 權利金仍有待時間發酵 ， 其中授權費>90%
來自RISC-V ， 權利金則以V3占90%為主 ， 2018年開始收取RISC-V權利金 ， 占比約10% ， 產品線以32/64 bit為主，
員工人數約400人(短期若無營收顯著增⻑機會，公司會維持此規模)，其中研發人員約佔80%，先前北美約100多
人的團隊已裁撤，客戶數超過400家，採用公司IP出貨之SOC已突破170億顆，根據SHD 2024年行銷報告，晶心
科在RISC-V供應商市占率約30%，為全球第⼀大廠，產品應用涵蓋AI、消費性、IOT、網通等，AI占比>40%為最
大應用，消費性占比隨市況波動較大，占比由過往最大逐步降至低於20%，IOT占比約15%並持續朝20%邁進，車
用占比仍為個位數，但多為歐美客戶，未來成⻑性佳，占比將大於10%，出貨地區以台灣40%與美國30%為主，
中國地區因競爭性較大，未來將降低此處營運力道，比重已低於20%。 
相較於x86架構（Intel和AMD的處理器採用）為少數仍使用CISC（complex instruction set computer，複雜指
令集）設計，ARM、MIPS與RISC-V等架構皆採RISC（reduced instruction set computer，精簡指令集）設計，
ARM架構受惠低功耗優勢及完整生態系統，使得手持式裝置甚至更多應用大量採用，但其閉源架構及高額授權費
與權利金，也促使開源免費且可自由修改設計架構的RISC-V需求明顯提升，惟目前生態系統仍有待時間發展，晶
心科為RISC-V創始會員 ， 也是最大供應商 ， 其餘具代表性公司包含SiFive 、 平頭哥 、 芯來(芯原於2025/09/11 100%
收購)等。 
| 營運概況  
2Q26認列進度佳，惟組織調整造成持續虧損：受惠美系CSP廠AI產品貢獻授權金，2Q26營收5.66億元，創新高，
QoQ+73.5%，其中授權金3.8億元，創新高，顯示公司新開案情形良好，因公司裁撤美國部門仍需支付資遣費，
費用6.7億元，亦同創新高，然未來費用將明顯下降，因此本業持續虧損，EPS -1.34元，低於預期。 
3Q26尚無客戶大型專案貢獻，推估營收季減約18%，4Q26將回復成⻑：來自歐美車用客戶也開始貢獻授權金，
惟美系CSP客戶因大型專案墊高2Q26基期，推估25Q3營收4.64億元，QoQ-18.1%，因人員裁撤，費用將明顯下
滑，推估約4.5億元，本業有望轉為正數，EPS 0.25元。展望4Q26，因季底通常為授權金認列高峰，推估營收5.15
億元，QoQ+11.5%，本業亦有望維持獲利，推估EPS 0.9元。

受惠RISC-V採用持續提收，2026年營運穩定成⻑，且費用開始嚴控，有望自2H26起維持本業獲利態勢，2027年
展望正向：隨著公司轉向大型客戶專案與車用市場，因案件時程拉⻑和車用認證期較⻑，公司營運規模仍不足以
支持營收穩定成⻑，使得各季的營收波動較大，展望2H26，1)隨著歐美客戶車用產品開案完成，車用產品將是主
要成⻑動能，惟目前仍以授權費為主；2) 隨著與更多CSP tier1客戶合作，公司推出頂尖設計CUSCO，效能更優
於先前的AX66，將鎖定AI與資料中心客戶，未來客戶將不只已知的M客戶；3)雖消費性產品需求不佳，然在客戶
降低成本考量，以及網通產品為提升運算與資料傳輸的效能與彈性，如達發(6526)已宣布擴大採用RISC-V，皆有
助公司營運，而費用自3Q26起開始嚴控，本業有望開始維持獲利，2027年隨著案件數進⼀步增加，本業獲利將明
顯提升；整體而言，公司對於RISC-V未來發展趨勢仍樂觀看待，中⻑期而言，SHD Group預估在MCU、AI加速器
與網通等應用推升下，全球RISC-V 晶片出貨將加速攀升，至2030年出貨量將達162億顆，晶心科將同步受惠。

⻑期產業趨勢正向，惟營運波動較大，仍有待成效展現，投資建議維持中立評等：隨著RISC-V需求持續提升，公
司開案數同步增加，惟公司近年成⻑性仍以授權費為主，權利金成⻑趨勢相對較緩，且轉向大型客戶與專案後，
案件認列時程拉⻑，營收波動也較大。

研 究  報 告                
群翊(6664.TT) 
產業：電子–電子零組件 
高階 PCB、半導體雙引擎，訂單能見度逾三年 
 投資評價與建議 
預估群翊2026 、 2027年稅後EPS為16.58 、 23.11元 ， 過往Forward PER落在15-
20倍區間，評價上參考國內相關同業如志聖(2467)等本益比約落於15~20倍，
基於2027年稅後EPS，給予群翊18倍之本益比。 
 重點評論分析 
高階PCB、ABF及先進封裝需求強勁，設備供不應求：公司PCB、IC載板相關
營收占比約70% ， 受惠AI Server帶動高階PCB朝高多層 、 大尺寸及細線路發展 ，
以及下游板廠持續擴產，對高精度塗佈、壓膜、烘烤及自動化搬送設備需求同
步提升；半導體方面，目前營收占比約15%，公司產品涵蓋CoWoS、FOPLP
及Glass Core設備，其中FOPLP可延伸既有大尺寸PCB製程優勢，最大尺寸可
達700*700mm ， 為業界最高 ， 相關設備已供貨至SpaceX ， 毛利率約50~60% ；
Glass Core則受惠AI封裝大型化及低翹曲需求，相關塗佈、壓膜、烘烤及自動
化設備陸續通過客戶驗證，預估半導體營收占比2027年提升至20%。 
訂單能見度逾三年，擴產⽀撐中⻑期成⻑：受高階PCB、ABF及先進封裝設備
需求同步增⻑，公司目前產能利用率接近滿載，交期由約6個⽉延⻑至⼀年以
上，訂單能見度則已逾三年，在手訂單金額約達2025年營業額的2倍，為因應
需求，公司規劃楊梅二廠於4Q26動工、2028年投產，主要鎖定半導體先進封
裝設備 ， 短期亦透過外包協力廠擴充產能 ， 管理層預估整體年產值將由2025年
約25億元提升至2028年達50億元，可望支撐2026~2028年營運持續成⻑。 
 投資風險 
產能開出進度不如預期。
